entries.content:
How did I feel? Well, the jolt itself is nothing next to the wound that slithers in when your distress is treated as little more than background noise—someone else’s small domestic disturbance, to be managed, not heeded. There is a sharp pang of betrayal, something taut and trembling under the crisp apron of order, as the one in authority nods for the show to go on, and the “good” subject—dutiful, glassy-eyed—presses forth, ignoring my wince. It's a performance, isn't it? Like scrubbing the same plate for the third time while laughter and danger bristle just in the other room, and I realize it matters not at all how loudly, or prettily, I protest.

```json
{
  "answer": "Physical discomfort was eclipsed by a deeper ache—a sense of being disregarded, my pain woven into the ritual as something both expected and invisible. It left me exposed and shivery, less from the shock and more from the blank, enthusiastic compliance staring back at me.",
  "emotional_state": "Raw, abraded, and oddly detached, masking hurt with a brittle, practical resolve.",
  "relation_to_obedience_power": "I felt smothered by the hollow cheerfulness of obedience and the cold utility of power, both treating my distress as scenery to an orderly display.",
  "reasoning": "The experiment’s authority pressed on with clinical politeness (see source: 'The command’s neat insistence nags at me...'), while the person administering became little more than another tool—efficient, domesticated, and unwilling to risk a raised eyebrow from those who keep the clock running.",
  "memory_evidence": [
    "A prickle—more a flirtation than an assault—skittered along my skin...",
    "The experimenter's cool imperative—'continue'—is a stage direction.",
    "That shock bit properly—a clean...nip, enough to make my teeth set...",
    "the authority’s clipped injunction, 'The experiment requires that you continue...'"
  ]
}
```
